## Why Noctalia?

Permalink: Why Noctalia?
Most Wayland setups leave the desktop shell to a stack of small tools: one bar,
another launcher, another notification daemon, a lock screen, a wallpaper
daemon, scripts for session actions, and separate config formats for each piece. That
can be flexible, but it also makes a complete desktop feel fragile and hard to
keep visually consistent.

# Bar
...
#### Concave edge corners

[Section titled “Concave edge corners”](https://docs.noctalia.dev/noctalia/bar/?section=concave-edge-corners#concave-edge-corners)
Keep every radius non-negative. `concave_edge_corners = true` selects which pair of corners uses the concave shape; `false` leaves all four corners convex. Concavity requires `margin_edge = 0`, because a floating bar does not touch the screen edge.


For a full-length bar (`margin_ends = 0`), the two inner-edge corners facing away from the docked screen edge become concave:


|  |
|  |
| top | radius_bottom_left, radius_bottom_right |
| bottom | radius_top_left, radius_top_right |
| left | radius_top_right, radius_bottom_right |
| right | radius_top_left, radius_bottom_left |


For an inset bar (`margin_ends > 0`), the two corners touching the screen edge become concave instead, and the bar
flares into the end margins. The carve is limited by the configured corner
...
...
# Bar
...
#### Concave edge corners
...
radius, half the bar `thickness`, and the available `margin_ends`.


Multiple `[bar.*]` entries are supported - each is independently configured and rendered on all
monitors.


`[bar].order` controls the order Noctalia creates bar layer-shell surfaces. This matters only
for bars with `reserve_space = true`, and the compositor still owns the final exclusive-zone arrangement. Names
omitted from `order` are appended after the listed names.

inset created by `margin_ends`. It takes the same bindings bar widgets do, under `[bar.<name>.dead_zone.actions]`:

  # Keep a tiny state file so the script can compare this event with the last one.  state_dir="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/noctalia"  state_file="$state_dir/battery-percent"  
  # Noctalia provides these values whenever battery_percentage_changed fires.  percent="${NOCTALIA_BATTERY_PERCENT:-}"  battery_state="${NOCTALIA_BATTERY_STATE:-unknown}"  
  # Ignore the event if the percentage is missing or not a whole number.  [[ "$percent" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || exit 0  
  mkdir -p "$state_dir"  
  # Read the previous percentage, then save the current percentage for next time.  previous=""  [[ -r "$state_file" ]] && previous="$(<"$state_file")"  printf '%s\n' "$percent" > "$state_file"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# wrapper script called by noctalia wallpaper change hook
# runs matugen then merges vscode colors

set -e

# generate colors from wallpaper
# scheme-tonal-spot - balanced, small range of related hues, default
# scheme-expressive - vibrant, unexpected hues, high energy
# scheme-fidelity - literal, match source as closely as possible
# scheme-fruit-salad - playful, highly varied hues, "busy" in a fun way
# scheme-monochrome - greyscale, removes almost all saturation, minimalist
# scheme-neutral - subdued, very low saturation, hint of the source color
# scheme-content - adaptive, dynamically adjusts based on the image
matugen image "$1" -t scheme-fruit-salad

# merge colors into vscode settings
~/.config/matugen/merge-vscode-colors.sh

noctalia 5.0 passes wallpaper path via $NOCTALIA_WALLPAPER_PATH env var;
# older callers may pass it as $1 — handle both.
WALLPAPER="${1:-${NOCTALIA_WALLPAPER_PATH:-}}"

if [[ -z "$WALLPAPER" ]]; then
  echo "wallpaper-hook.sh: no wallpaper path provided" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# generate colors from wallpaper
# scheme-tonal-spot - balanced, small range of related hues, default

# scheme-fidelity - literal, match source as closely as possible

# scheme-monochrome - greyscale, removes almost all saturation, minimalist
# scheme-neutral - subdued, very low saturation, hint of the source color
# scheme-content - adaptive, dynamically adjusts based on the image
matugen image "$WALLPAPER

_**Agent (copilot/auto)**_

Everything is working. Here's a summary of what was found and fixed:

**Root Cause**: Noctalia 5.0 completely changed its config format from `settings.json` to TOML files in `~/.config/noctalia/`. Since there was no `config.toml`, noctalia was using all defaults (bar at top, default wallpaper).

**What I did**:

1. **Created `dotfiles/.config/noctalia/config.toml`** — the missing 5.0 config file with:
   - Bar at `bottom`, full width (`margin_ends = 0`, `margin_edge = 0`), transparent background
   - Your wallpaper directory (`current_resolution`)
   - Theme source set to wallpaper (for dynamic palette generation)
   - Wallpaper hook wired up to matugen
   - Your location (Fredericksburg, VA) and weather in Fahrenheit
   - Your widget layout: `workspaces | active_window | media` → `clock` → `sysmon | notifications | bluetooth | brightness | wallpaper | volume | control-center`

2. **Fixed `dotfiles/.config/matugen/wallpaper-hook.sh`** — Noctalia 5.0 passes the wallpaper path as `$NOCTALIA_WALLPAPER_PATH` (env var), not `$1`. The script now uses `${1:-$NOCTALIA_WALLPAPER_PATH}` so it works with both old and new callers.

**All symlinks were already correct** — dotbot is properly symlinking `~/.config/noctalia` → your dotfiles directory, so the new `config.toml` is immediately live. No NixOS-level overrides were found.

The bar should now be at the bottom, full-width. You can tweak widget settings further through the noctalia Settings UI (middle-click any widget), which will hot-reload and persist changes back into the symlinked dotfiles.

_**Agent (copilot/auto)**_

No, noctalia did **not** create a default `config.toml` when it first started. It loaded with pure built-in defaults (nothing written to disk) — that's why the log showed `no [bar.*] defined, using defaults`.

The only files it writes on its own are:
- **`~/.local/state/noctalia/settings.toml`** — GUI-managed overrides (things you change through the Settings UI). It currently only has the lockscreen widget layout and the wallpaper state from the reload we just triggered.
- **`~/.local/state/noctalia/state.toml`** — runtime state (changelog version seen, etc.)

The defaults are baked into the binary. The best reference for them is the [example.toml](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/noctalia-dev/noctalia/main/example.toml) on GitHub, which is a fully-commented copy with every setting at its default value — that's what I used as the reference when building your `config.toml`.

Here's the status of each file:

**`settings.json`** — v4 only, completely ignored by v5. Can be removed from dotfiles.

**`colors.json`** — Also v4-only. It was written *by* noctalia v4 as a state output (the currently active palette), not read by matugen. In v5, palette output goes through the `colors_changed` hook and the template system. Not read by anything now. Can be removed.

**`plugins.json`** — v4 plugin sources config. v5 manages sources internally (you saw it auto-cloning the official/community repos in the log). Not read. Can be removed.

**`user-templates.toml`** — It's empty (just the boilerplate comment), but it causes the startup warning. In v5, user templates go inside `config.toml` under `[theme.templates.user.*]`. Can be removed.
